message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| **1** | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| **2** | **Gather Parts** | All components must fit together. | Check compatibility: motherboard socket, RAM type, GPU length, PSU wattage. |
| **3** | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Use an anti‑static wrist strap or work on a non‑conductive mat. |
| **4** | **Open the Case** | Access the interior. | Remove side panels; keep screws handy. |
| **5** | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to everything. | Place it in the designated spot (usually bottom or top). Secure with screws. |
| **6** | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all components. | Align standoffs with holes; screw lightly. |
| **7** | **Install the CPU** | Core of performance. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock latch. |
| **8** | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Prevent overheating. | Use a pea‑size amount; spread evenly. Attach cooler per its instructions. |
| **9** | **Insert RAM** | Memory for multitasking. | Snap sticks into DIMM slots; ensure they click. |
| **10** | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into the M.2 slot and screw. For 2.5”/3.5” drives, use drive bays or brackets. |
| **11** | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Visual output & gaming. | Insert into the top PCI‑e x16 slot; secure with screws. |
| **12** | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | PSU 24‑pin to motherboard, 8‑pin CPU power, GPU power connectors, SATA power for drives. |
| **13** | **Connect Data Cables** | Data flow. | SATA data cables to motherboard, M.2 connector already seated. |
| **14** | **Cable Management** | Airflow & aesthetics. | Tuck cables behind the motherboard tray; use zip ties. |
| **15** | **Check Connections** | Avoid shorts or missing power. | Verify all screws, cables, and standoffs are secure. |
| **16** | **Close the Case** | Protect components. | Reattach side panels, tighten screws. |
| **17** | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Confirm hardware detection. | Power on, enter BIOS (usually DEL/F2). Check CPU, RAM, storage, GPU. Update BIOS if needed. |
| **18** | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Functional PC. | Create a bootable USB (Windows, Linux, etc.), boot from it, follow installation steps. |
| **19** | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Optimal performance. | Install motherboard chipset drivers, GPU drivers, Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth drivers. |
| **20** | **Test & Benchmark** | Verify stability. | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, etc.) and monitor temperatures. |

---

## Detailed Tips & Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Static Damage** | Ground yourself before touching components. |
| **CPU Not Seating** | Ensure the CPU is aligned correctly; the triangle marker must match the socket. |
| **GPU Too Long** | Check case clearance; some GPUs exceed 300 mm. |
| **Insufficient PSU Wattage** | Use an online PSU calculator; add a 20–30 % safety margin. |
| **Poor Airflow** | Keep front intake fans, rear exhaust fans, and optionally top exhaust. |
| **Cable Clutter** | Use Velcro straps or zip ties; route cables along the back of the motherboard tray. |
| **BIOS Not Detecting GPU** | Make sure the GPU is fully seated and power connectors are attached. |
| **No POST (Power On Self Test)** | Double‑check all power connections, especially the 24‑pin and 8‑pin CPU connectors. |

---

## Quick Reference: Component Compatibility Checklist

| Component | Key Specs to Match |
|-----------|--------------------|
| **CPU** | Socket type (e.g., LGA1200, AM4), chipset support |
| **Motherboard** | Socket, RAM type (DDR4/DDR5), form factor (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX) |
| **RAM** | Speed (MHz), capacity, dual‑channel support |
| **GPU** | PCI‑e slot (x16), length, power connectors |
| **Storage** | M.2 NVMe vs SATA, 2.5” vs 3.5” |
| **PSU** | Wattage, 80+ rating, connector types |
| **Case** | Size (ATX, micro‑ATX, mini‑ITX), GPU clearance, PSU mounting |

---

## Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & compatibility checker.  
- **YouTube Channels** – *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* for visual guides.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and GPU manuals for specific instructions.  

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over performance and aesthetics. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
